key_insight: A Task-Similarity Network (TSN) computes affinity between a new offline task and previously learned tasks to drive selective parameter reuse, enabling effective continual learning from offline datasets while reducing catastrophic forgetting.
problem_solved: Enables continual offline reinforcement learning (CORL) — learning a sequence of tasks from datasets collected over time — by addressing catastrophic forgetting and inefficient transfer when online interaction is costly or impossible.
method: Train a Task-Similarity Network (TSN) to produce affinity scores between the current task dataset and stored task representations.
Use affinity-guided parameter reuse: selectively freeze, reuse, or adapt model parameters from prior tasks according to similarity (via masks, routing, or weighted regularization).
Optimize with offline RL objectives while prioritizing high-affinity parameter reuse to preserve prior-task performance without extensive replay or online interaction.
impact: Provides a practical way to adapt RL agents to new offline tasks safely and efficiently, improving retention of past skills and reducing need for costly or risky environment interactions. This aids deployment in real-world, interaction-constrained domains.
visual_elements: Affinity heatmap: matrix of TSN similarity scores between new task and past tasks (warm colors = high reuse).
Model pipeline diagram: dataset → TSN → affinity scores → selective parameter reuse (highlight frozen vs adapted modules).
Performance timeline: episodic bar/line chart showing retained returns on past tasks vs baseline continual methods (illustrating reduced forgetting).
Bar chart or table: average return and forgetting metric comparisons across methods (TSN-Affinity vs replay / regularization baselines).
paper_title: TSN-Affinity: Similarity-Driven Parameter Reuse for Continual Offline Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Dominik Żurek, Kamil Faber, Marcin Pietron, Paweł Gajewski, Roberto Corizzo
